Class ACurve

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.splot.pdata.ACurve
Direct Known Subclasses:
Curve, HistoCurve, StripChartCurve
public abstract class ACurve extends Object
Base class for all plottable curves (XY curves, histogram curves, strip-chart curves, etc.).

Responsibilities

  • State: name, visibility, style, drawing method, per-curve fit “order” knob.
  • Computed artifacts: fit results/evaluator and spline cache.
  • Notifications: curve-level change events for data/style/fit.
  • Batching: coalescing multiple changes into a single notification burst.

Thread-safety policy

This library is Swing-based. Curve change notifications commonly lead (directly or indirectly) to repaint() on a plot canvas. Swing requires UI updates to occur on the Event Dispatch Thread (EDT). Therefore:

  • All methods that notify listeners must be called on the EDT.
  • Data integrity within a curve is typically protected by lock in subclasses, but lock does not make Swing notifications thread-safe by itself.

For streaming / DAQ scenarios, the recommended pattern is: 

producer threads → enqueue points (lock-free queue) → EDT drains → curve.add(...)

Dirty flag and cache invalidation

The curve may cache computed artifacts such as a FitResult or CubicSpline. When data or relevant rendering parameters change, those artifacts must be invalidated and the curve marked dirty.

Use:

  • markDataChanged() when the underlying data values have changed.
  • markStyleChanged() when appearance or drawing configuration has changed.
  • markFitChanged() when a fit result has been updated (e.g., after doFit(boolean)).

  • Field Details

    • lock

      protected final Object lock
      Lock object intended for subclasses to synchronize data mutation and snapshot creation.

      This lock is about data consistency (e.g., keeping x/y arrays aligned). It does not automatically make Swing notifications safe; notifications are enforced to be EDT-only.

    • clearData

      public abstract void clearData()
      Clear all data from this curve and fire a DATA change event.

      Thread-safe: may be called from any thread. If called off the EDT, the clear is performed later on the EDT and coalesced with other scheduled drains.

      Note: this also clears any queued (not-yet-applied) points so the curve truly becomes empty.

    • beginUpdate

      public final void beginUpdate()
      Begin batching curve change notifications.

      While batching (depth > 0), calls to fireCurveChanged(CurveChangeType) do not notify listeners immediately; instead they set pending flags. When endUpdate() returns the depth to 0, pending flags are flushed.

      Must be called on the EDT.

    • endUpdate

      public final void endUpdate()
      End batching curve change notifications.

      When the batch depth returns to 0, pending changes are flushed. Must be called on the EDT.

    • scheduleDrainOnce

      protected final void scheduleDrainOnce(Runnable drainOnEdt)
      Schedule a drain operation to run later on the Swing EDT, coalescing multiple requests into a single posted runnable.

      This is intended for curves whose add(...) methods are safe to call from any thread: background calls enqueue data, then call this method to ensure the queued data is applied on the EDT.

      If many threads call this repeatedly, only the first call posts a runnable; subsequent calls are coalesced until the posted runnable begins execution.

      Parameters:
      drainOnEdt - code that must execute on the EDT (typically calls drainPendingOnEDT(...) in the subclass)
